cue: Describe a person who helped you at an important time in your life.
bullets: what they did to help you
last: and explain why their help was so important to you.
part3: In what ways do people in your community usually help each other?
Why do some people find it difficult to ask for help?
Do you think people are less willing to help strangers than they were in the past?
Should children learn to help others at school, or is that mainly the family's job?
What responsibility do governments have to support people who are going through hard times?

cue: Describe a colleague or classmate you enjoy working with.
bullets: how long you have known them
what kind of work you do together
last: and explain why you enjoy working with this person.
part3: What makes someone a good team member?
Do you think people generally work better alone or in a team?
How important is it to be friends with the people you work with?
Why do conflicts sometimes happen between colleagues, and how should they be handled?
Have relationships at work changed now that many people work from home?
What can employers do to create a positive atmosphere in the workplace?

cue: Describe a city you would like to live and work in one day.
bullets: what kind of work you would like to do there
last: and explain why you would like to live and work in this city.
part3: Why do so many young people move from small towns to big cities?
What are the advantages and disadvantages of living in a capital city?
Is it better to build a career in your own country or abroad?
What problems can arise when too many people move to the same city?
How do you think cities will change over the next twenty years?
Should governments encourage companies to open offices outside the main cities?

cue: Describe a quiet place where you like to spend time.
last: and explain why you like spending time in this place.
part3: Why do people sometimes need to be somewhere quiet?
Is it harder to find peace and quiet in cities today than it was in the past?
How serious a problem is noise pollution in your country?
What can city planners do to create more peaceful public spaces?
Some people say we have lost the ability to be alone with our own thoughts. Do you agree?

cue: Describe a piece of technology you use every day.
last: and explain how your life would be different without it.
part3: What kinds of technology do older people in your country find difficult to use?
How has technology changed the way people work?
Do you think children today depend too much on technology?
Is it a good thing that employers can now contact their staff at any time of day?
Will new technology create more jobs than it takes away in the future?

cue: Describe a time you solved a difficult problem at work or in your studies.
last: and explain how you felt after solving it.
part3: What kinds of problems do people most often face at work?
Is it better to solve a problem on your own or to ask others for advice?
Why do some people stay calm under pressure while others panic?
Do schools do enough to teach young people how to solve problems?
In which jobs is the ability to solve problems most important, and why?
How might artificial intelligence change the way people solve problems at work?

cue: Describe a celebration that you particularly enjoyed.
bullets: where and when it took place
last: and explain why you enjoyed it so much.
part3: What are the most important celebrations in your country?
Why do some families spend so much money on weddings and other celebrations?
How have the ways people celebrate changed since your grandparents' time?
What are the benefits of celebrating success at work?
Do you think traditional festivals will still matter to people in the future?

cue: Describe a useful skill you learned after you left school.
bullets: how and where you learned it
whether it was difficult to learn
last: and explain how this skill has helped you.
part3: What skills should young people learn before they start working?
Is it easier for children or for adults to learn new skills?
How has the internet changed the way people learn practical skills?
Should employers pay for their staff to learn new skills?
Which skills do you think will be most valuable in twenty years' time?

cue: Describe a healthy habit you have.
bullets: how you manage to keep it up
last: and explain how this habit has affected your health.
part3: What are some common unhealthy habits in your country?
Why do many people find it so hard to change their habits?
Are people today healthier than people were fifty years ago?
How can workplaces encourage their employees to live more healthily?
Who should be responsible for people's health: individuals or the government?
Should advertising for unhealthy food and drinks be restricted?

cue: Describe a plan you have for the next few years.
bullets: what you need to do to achieve it
last: and explain why this plan is important to you.
part3: Do you think it is important for young people to plan their future?
Why do some people prefer not to make long-term plans?
How do people's goals tend to change as they get older?
How much should parents influence their children's choice of career?
Is the idea of having one job for life disappearing, and is that a good thing?

cue: Describe a time you changed your mind about something important.
bullets: what you had planned to do at first
what made you change your mind
last: and say whether you think you made the right choice.
part3: What kinds of decisions do young people find most difficult?
Who do people in your country usually turn to for advice before a big decision?
Is changing your mind a sign of weakness or a sign of strength?
How much does social media influence the decisions people make?
Should political leaders change their policies when public opinion changes?

cue: Describe a website or app that you find useful.
bullets: what it is and how you found out about it
last: and explain why you find it so useful.
part3: What kinds of apps are most popular with people in your country?
Do older and younger people use the internet in different ways?
Is it a good idea for people to look for health advice online?

Should companies be allowed to collect data about how people use their apps?
